g.text: SOTA: how today's models and serving engines handle the KV cache
KV / token = 2 * L * H_kv * d_h * S (MLA: L * (d_c + d_R) * S) | configs from public model cards / papers, sizes derived in BF16 (S = 2 B) | companion: comparison.excalidraw, serving_stack.excalidraw
1. What frontier open models actually cache (per token, all layers, BF16)
DeepSeek-V3: 576 * 2 B * 61 = 70,272 B = 68.6 KiB/token. The same model as plain MHA would cache 2*61*128*128*2 B = 3.8 MiB/token (57x more).
A 671B-parameter MLA model caches LESS per token than an 8B GQA model (68.6 vs 128 KiB): architecture beats size for KV.
Layer-mix designs cut the T-growing part: Gemma-3 = 5 local (1,024-token window) : 1 global layer; Jamba = 1 attention : 7 Mamba layers;
Qwen3-Next = 3 Gated-DeltaNet : 1 gated-attention layer -> only 1/6, 1/8, 1/4 of layers keep a KV cache that grows with T.
2. The SOTA toolbox, grouped by the problem each tool attacks
3. Worked example: 32K-token chats, 100 GB of HBM set aside for KV (= 93.1 GiB)
chats that fit (93.1 GiB / per chat)
MHA shape for Llama-3-70B: 2 * 80 * 64 * 128 * 2 B = 2,621,440 B = 2.5 MiB / token.
MLA: 70,272 B * 32,768 = 2.30e9 B = 2.15 GiB. FP8 KV halves S: 1.07 GiB.
This is KV ONLY: DeepSeek-V3 weights (671B params, ~671 GB in FP8) need a
multi-GPU node, Llama-3-70B ~140 GB in BF16. Compare per KV budget, not per GPU.
Batch size = concurrency = throughput: 9 -> 43 -> 86 chats in the same 100 GB.
4. A 2025-26 reference serving stack (top = what the model decides, bottom = what the hardware gives)
GQA or MLA attention, local/global or linear-hybrid layers, MoE FFN, FP8 / INT4 weights
vLLM / SGLang / TensorRT-LLM: continuous batching, chunked prefill, prefix cache, speculative decoding
paged KV blocks + block table, FP8 KV cache, radix / prefix sharing, CPU / SSD offload tiers
FlashAttention-3 (Hopper), FlashInfer (paged, ragged), FlashMLA, fused RoPE / quantize
tensor parallel within a node, expert parallel for MoE, prefill/decode disaggregation, context parallel for 1M ctx
H100 80 GB 3.35 TB/s | H200 141 GB 4.8 TB/s | B200 192 GB 8 TB/s (capacity and bandwidth both limit KV)
5. Symptom -> which SOTA tool to reach for first
OOM / tiny batch at long context
GQA or MLA model, FP8 KV, offload, context parallel
KV bytes per token x T is the wall
low throughput, VRAM 'full' but few seqs
thousands of chats share a system prompt
chunked prefill, prefix cache, context parallel
hybrid / linear layers, sliding window, ring attention
full KV for every layer does not fit
Snapshot of public configs and papers as of 2025-26: verify a model card before quoting its numbers in production.
The constant across all of it: KV bytes = 2 * L * B * T * H_kv * d_h * S. Every SOTA tool attacks one term, its placement, or how fast it is read.
